commentary:
Energy owns the tape this morning. The US and Iran traded tanker attacks over the weekend and Tehran says it will declare a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, stoking fears of prolonged disruption to flows through the waterway — Brent is up 1.2% at $97.4 and WTI 1.2% at $92.6, with OPEC+ holding quotas unchanged even as the war shutters swathes of Mideast output. The real strain is in products: heating oil +1.9% and gasoil +2.3%, with a Ukrainian strike on Rosneft's big Ryazan refinery tightening distillates further, and TTF gas up 3.6%.

Diesel is the spoiler for inflation doves — crude futures arguably still aren't reflecting physical tightness. That feeds directly into an already hawkish rates picture. A hot jobs report has lifted Fed hike odds, talk of an ECB "insurance" hike is circulating, and the structural forces behind the bond reset — sticky inflation, heavy government issuance — aren't letting up. Treasuries, Bunds, OATs and gilts are all offered, long end leading, with the AfD's German state-election win adding a political wrinkle for European duration.

Higher real rates are trumping geopolitics in metals: gold is off 0.5% despite the Hormuz escalation, silver and copper softer too. The exception to the cautious tone is Asia, where tech strength drove the Nikkei up 2% and KOSPI 4.6%; US and European index futures are flat-to-soft. Elsewhere, China's $45bn bank recapitalization plan is supporting iron ore (+1.1%), while grains are broadly lower — CBOT wheat down 2.7% — and robusta coffee firm.
